summary: Dedicated: intermittent 5xx during pool validation window on capacity expansion (new nodes/pool briefly routed before Ready)
description:
Customer report
- BrightLedger reported intermittent 5xx errors during a Dedicated capacity expansion window.
- Symptom: bursts of 5xx (mostly upstream 502/503) for ~8–12 minutes, then self-resolved.
- Customer observed errors only on a subset of requests; overall latency remained normal outside error windows.

Impact
- Customer-facing errors in production during their business hours.
- Approx impact (from edge + routing metrics): ~0.6–0.9% request failure rate during the window; concentrated to one pool.
- No data loss; retries generally succeeded.

Environment / scope
- Dedicated pool expansion in us-east.
- Expansion was running the new provision-to-ready automation pilot (validation/perf-canary gating).

Initial triage notes (Support + SRE)
- Hypothesis: new nodes were briefly advertised to routing before readiness checks completed, causing transient failures while runtime/bootstrap was still in progress.
- Confirmed: routing logs show a short period where pool state was effectively treated as usable while it was still in Validating (or “Ready” was set prematurely).

What we saw (evidence)
- Routing:
  - Error spike aligned with increase in traffic share to newly-added capacity.
  - 5xx signatures: upstream connection resets + occasional TLS handshake failures to data plane endpoints.
- Control plane:
  - Provisioning run shows state transition into Ready before perf-canary completion timestamp.
  - Subsequent validation step failures (GPU health + runtime smoke) occurred after some traffic was already flowing.
- Infra/provisioning:
  - Nodes were still converging on final helm values during the time window.

Mitigation applied (during incident)
- Immediately removed new capacity from routing advertisement (keep pool out of routing until Ready is unequivocally true):
  - Forced routing to use prior stable nodes only.
  - Paused the provisioning run at Validating to prevent flapping.
- Customer comms: acknowledged incident, advised retry/backoff for a short window; confirmed mitigation in place and errors subsiding.

Root cause (most likely)
- Race condition between control-plane “Ready” state setting and completion of perf-canary readiness suite.
- Result: pool (or new shard) could be considered eligible by routing while still in validation.

Resolution
- Short-term: manual gating (exclude the new capacity from routing) until validation suite passed.
- Code fix: merged fix to prevent Ready being set before perf-canary completion + added transactional check in state transition.
  - See PR: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/48245
- Confirmed: after fix and re-run of validation, no further 5xx bursts observed in the next 24 hours.

Follow-ups / action items
1) Ensure routing consumes ONLY Ready (never Validating) across all Dedicated pools.
   - PR reference: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/48234
2) Add alert for “traffic to pool not Ready” and “Ready set before perf-canary finished” invariant violation.
   - Dashboard/alerts: https://github.com/redwood/observability-pack/pull/1204
3) Update operator runbook: explicit step to verify Ready gating before enabling routing; include checks/commands.
   - Confluence: eng-infra/runbooks/dedicated-pool-provisioning-runbook
4) Customer-facing messaging template for expansions: clarify that validation window keeps capacity out of routing to avoid partial readiness exposure.

Customer-facing note (for CS)
- We identified a sequencing bug that allowed a small slice of traffic to hit the new capacity before validation finished. We mitigated by keeping new capacity out of routing until checks passed, and we shipped a fix so this cannot happen going forward. We will continue monitoring and will schedule expansions to minimize customer-visible risk.

Links
- Slack incident thread: #incidents (ref: 1709135111)
- Ready-state troubleshooting: confluence: eng-platform/runbooks/control-plane-ready-state-troubleshooting
